newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: 3i to invest S$250 mln in Asia.
newsitem.headline: 3i to invest S$250 mln in Asia.

text.p: British investment company 3i Group Plc said on Tuesday it was planning to spend Singapore $250 of its own money on initial investments in Southeast Asia.

Announcing the opening of a new regional office in Singapore, 3i managing director for Southeast Asia Jane Crawford said the company was looking for investments in growing companies and value-added business-to-business sectors.
These would include the information technology, telecommunications, manufacturing and distribution industries, the company said in a statement.
The investments were expected to be made in amounts ranging from S$1.5 million to S$15 million, the statement said.

"3i is a value growth investor which is investing its own funds in Asia, not managing funds on behalf of others. This means we do not need to seek short-term realisation of our investments," the statement quoted Crawford as saying.

It said 3i would focus on providing expansion finance for growing businesses, management buy-ins -- with 3i providing the risk finance to allow new management teams to take over -- and management buy-outs, where existing managements take over.
